Subject: RFP follow-up — detailed soak testing & reservation phasing

Marissa, thanks for the RFP response — a couple of asks came out of our internal review.

1) We want a concrete soak-test plan (24/48/72h) that stresses long-tail latency (p99.9) with our mix: 45% chat (avg context 512), 35% short gen (avg 64), 20% embeddings (single request).
2) A phased commit (3 steps) where we can tier up over 6 months with an option to pause or step-down if regressions occur.
3) Need explicit GPU-family sensitivity: H100 vs A100 vs L4 — for each, give expected tokens/s, p50/p95/p99 latency at 256-token avg, and recommended quantization profile.

Can you provide a workbook and a runbook template we can use to approve the commitment internally? Also attach any SLA exception forms we need for cloud-burst lanes.

Carlos
Head of Platform Engineering
Helios AI
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — detailed soak testing & reservation phasing

Carlos — thanks, great questions. High level answer and attaching the workbook + templates.

Quick summary:
- We propose a three-phase commit: Pilot (4 wks, dev capacity), Ramp (3 months, 40% commit), Steady (month 4+, 100% target per agreed runrate). Option to pause at Ramp checkpoint with 30-day notice.
- Soak plan: 24h functional, 72h production soak with progressive load: 25%/50%/100% of target throughput over 72h and tail-focused sampling windows.
- GPU sensitivity: we include measured tokens/s and latency curves per family in the workbook. Short summary: H100 (best throughput for long contexts), A100 (balanced), L4 (cost-efficient for short context/embeddings). Recommended quantization: nf4 for A100/H100 for best quality/cost balance; int8 aggressive for L4-based embeddings-only profiles.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-gpu-sensitivity-workbook-v1.xlsx, soak-test-runbook-templates.pdf, sla-exception-request-form.docx

Next step: we'll run an initial 48h soak in our staging fleet with your dataset sample (if you can share). Otherwise we can run with synthetic load generator. Recommended dates: Jun 21-23 for first soak.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Priya — added operational detail below; pulled from the workbook (see tab: Billing & Fallback).

- Burst billing: Ramp includes 20% burst allowance per month. Bursts beyond allowance billed at on-demand list; we can cap monthly overage per contract (proposal: 15% overage cap).
- Spot fallback: available as a 'cost-optimise' lane. When on-demand capacity constrained we route to spot-compatible quantized variants (nf4-int8 mixed) with an expected ~10-15% latency inflation. Spot lanes are best-effort and excluded from hard SLOs unless specifically contracted. We provide an SLA exception form for guaranteed spot-backed lanes (attached).
- Pre-warm: typical KV cache pre-warm for conversational workloads is 5-15 minutes at steady warmup; for cold-start to warm cache we recommend a 1–3 hour proactive pre-warm for large context conversational workloads. We capture estimated hit ratios: 30% prefix cache hit for first-request heavy flows; 60–75% for steady-state conversational sessions when token overlap is high.

Operational ask: please share a representative 48h sample of your production trace (anonymized) or confirm we should proceed with synthetic traffic. If synthetic, we'll use our raven-loadgen harness with sequences 64/256/1024 across the soak windows.

Thanks — attaching the billing excerpt and runbook fragment.

--
Marissa

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — detailed soak testing & reservation phasing

Carlos — quick technical reply inline: answers and the SRE checklist below.

1) H100 vs A100 tokens/s (conversational, avg 512 tokens, low-latency mode, batch_size=1-4):
- H100-80GB (fp16, nf4 quant candidate): ~180–220 tokens/s per GPU at bs=1, ~400–480 tokens/s at bs=4 (best for long contexts due to larger HBM and kernel parallelism).
- A100-40GB (fp16, nf4 viable): ~120–150 tokens/s per GPU at bs=1, ~260–320 tokens/s at bs=4.
- L4-48GB (int8-optimized for short contexts): ~35–60 tokens/s at bs=1 for long contexts (not ideal), but very cost-effective for short generations and embeddings (embeddings: ~120–200 requests/s).

Kernel notes: H100 benefits from 3rd-party fused-attention kernels and more aggressive GEMM parallelism for seq>1024. A100 shows slightly tighter memory pressure on kv-cache; quantization to nf4 reduces memory footprint but requires careful calibration to avoid quality drift.

2) SRE failover checklist (72h soak):
- Alerts to instrument: p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency per model shard, GPU util, host memory used, KV cache hit rate, request queue depth, tail token generation rate. - Immediate mitigations (ordered): 1) Drop batch_size to 1; 2) Switch traffic to quantized variant (nf4) with automatic quality gating; 3) Redirect non-critical routes to spot lane; 4) Scale up reserved pool (if headroom exists) or trigger contracted burst.
- Rollback checklist: snapshot current model config, flip traffic to previous model variant, invalidate warmed KV cache if corrupted, purge long-tail requests older than 15s, and open a high-priority incident with the assigned infra lead.

We’ll include these rows in the workbook and map them to contract checkpoints so Ramp-phase suspension is operationally possible.

Let us know when the Drive link is up and any constraints for confidential traces (we can accept hashed/aggregated traces).

—Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
